title: Modular VPC Provisioner: exchangeable subnet profiles, smart-egress adapters, and rolling-upgrade safety net
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a reusable Terraform module (and companion policy/automation) for provisioning VPC networking for Private deployments. The module must support: multiple subnet profiles (control/data/infra), pluggable egress adapters (NAT gateway, managed egress appliance, IGW), region-aware VPC endpoints, intent-driven routing tables, and a rolling upgrade path with automated health checks and safe fallback. Goal: enable customers to deploy private Redwood clusters with minimal templates while giving platform teams safe upgrade primitives and observable health signals.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Terraform module can create a VPC with 3 subnet types (public control, private compute, restricted infra) via input profile selection
A2: Egress adapter abstraction implemented so infra teams can select 'nat-gw', 'igw', or 'egress-appliance' without changing top-level templates
A3: Module creates VPC endpoints for S3/EC2/SSM (configurable list) and exposes endpoint route maps in outputs
A4: Routing table provisioning supports intent tags so subnets inherit correct routes for cross-az HA and NAT failover
A5: Built-in health-check loop (external controller or Terraform-driven sentinel) runs synthetic egress probes and reports pass/fail in state outputs and a monitoring topic
A6: Rolling upgrade procedure documented and codified: canary apply to a subset of subnets, automated probe verification, automatic rollback on degraded metrics
A7: Module includes thorough example usage for private deployment templates and a migration recipe for existing private VPCs
design_notes: We treat subnet profiles as first-class input: users supply a small profile name which expands into cidr_mask, az_allocation_strategy, routable_to_control_plane boolean, and nat_needed boolean

Egress adapter is an interface pattern: implement provider-specific resources behind a single module output (egress_public_ip, egress_role_arn, egress_health_endpoint). Default implementations: AWS NAT Gateway (high-availability with elastic IPs) and IGW for lightweight customers
VPC endpoints are created via a configurable list; endpoints create private-route entries and security group attachments where applicable
Routing is 'intent-driven': an extra tags map on subnets and route tables allows us to map traffic classes (control-plane, telemetry, model-data) to next-hops and NACL policies

Upgrade safety model: staged applies driven by a small orchestration wrapper (Terraform plan/app scripts + a lightweight controller that executes health probes and gatekeeping) to enable canary->expand->full rollout

Health checks: prefer an external small agent (lambda/k8s job) that invokes documented probes: TCP connect to egress endpoint, HTTP probe to S3 endpoint via VPC endpoint, and traceroute-style path assertions. Probe results persisted to SNS and wrapped in a dashboard query
implementation_tasks: T1: Scaffold module with inputs/outputs and subnet profile expansion logic
T2: Implement egress_adapter submodule with 'nat-gw' and 'igw' implementations
T3: Endpoint creation submodule with conditional resources and endpoint-route binding
T4: Intent-route table generator: map tags to route blocks and create route resource per AZ
T5: Add outputs that enumerate important IDs for downstream modules (subnet_ids, route_table_map, egress_config)
T6: Build a lightweight rollout helper script (Python) that: applies canary, triggers probes, evaluates SLOs, and proceeds or rolls back
T7: Unit tests and terraform validate in CI, plus a k8s/lambda probe harness for integration tests
T8: Documentation page and example templates for private deployment onboarding
testing_plan: Unit: terraform fmt, validate, and tflint runs; small mocked plan tests for each adapter
Integration: spin up a small ephemeral account VPC with 2 AZs, deploy module with nat-gw and run probe harness
Chaos: simulate NAT gateway failure (delete elastic IP) and assert automatic failover route behavior and probe failures cause canary rollback
Upgrade smoke: run the rollout helper to perform a canary change (eg. modify MTU or route preference) and validate probe pass/fail behavior
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Merge module code behind feature flag and land on staging registry
Stage 1 (Canary): Use rollout helper to apply changes to 1 AZ subnet group in our staging-private account; run probes for 30m
Stage 2 (Expand): If probes stable, expand to remaining AZs; continue monitoring for 2h
Stage 3 (GA): Publish module version, add to Private Deploy starter template, notify solutions and SE teams
Rollback: rollout helper will run 'terraform apply' to revert to prior state and send an incident note to #private-deploy-alerts if probe threshold exceeded
risks: IAM complexity: creating endpoints and egress roles may require delicate permissions and cross-account assumptions
State drift: teams modifying route tables outside the module could lead to non-deterministic behavior during upgrades
Probe correctness: synthetic probes might have false positives if upstream services change behavior
Cost: NAT gateways and cross-AZ data egress can materially increase customer bills if not properly sized
Rollback safety: Terraform state-only rollbacks can be insufficient if resources were destroyed externally
